title: Structured acceptance quilt: tagging, risk buffers, and auto-defer policy for new model variants
creator: Priya Rao
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers increasingly submit model variant requests that vary widely in latency, cost, compatibility, and regulatory requirements. The current intake queue mixes critical low-latency customer pins with exploratory research variants, causing slow SLAs, missed deadlines for sensitive customers, and unscoped review work for infra and compliance. Goal: introduce a deterministic triage rubric and automated routing that tags incoming model requests, applies risk buffers, and auto-defers low-priority variants. This reduces average time-to-first-review for high-SLA customers to <48 hours and decreases manual review churn for the product and infra teams by ~30%. Scope: intake form, auto-scorer, routing lanes (latency-tiered, compliance-flagged, sandbox), reviewer handoff rules, and a minimal UI for triage notes in the Console. Non-goals: building full automated evals or replacing manual compliance decisions for regulated models. Success metrics: median time-to-first-review for P0/P1 requests, percent of requests auto-deferred, reviewer hours saved per week.
acceptance_criteria: New intake form captures latency sensitivity, cost delta, residency/compliance constraints, and backward-compatibility risk
Auto-scorer tags requests into L1 (low-latency), L2 (throughput-tolerant), Sandbox, or Compliance-Review lanes with >=85% alignment to manual triage on a 200-sample blind set
Dashboard shows per-lane SLA attainment and pending queue counts
Auto-defer policy moves tags with score < 25 to deferred-sandbox and notifies requestor with clear next steps
proposed_workflow: Intake: customer fills enhanced catalog request form (new fields added)
Auto-scorer: rule-based + ML heuristic assigns lane and initial priority
Human review: assigned PM/Eng reviewer validates tags within SLA window (48h for P0/P1)
Routing: approved -> staging-sandbox -> canary -> pin request OR deferred with guidance
scoring_factors: Compatibility break risk (inferred from API/embedding changes) (weight 15%)
artifacts_required: Minimal eval set (10–50 prompts representative of customer workload)
Performance smoke test script (latency P50/P95 for 16–512 tokens)
Recommended quantization profile or model size suggestion
rollout_plan: Shadowing for 48–72h against production traffic for compatibility-sensitive requests
Canary at 5–10% traffic for 24–72h with rollback hooks
Staged pin: incremental increase guarded by regression thresholds
Fallback: automated reroute to compatible variant on latency or reply-error SLO breach
monitoring_signals: Quality regressions on held eval prompts (top-k prompt drift)
Customer-facing error/incident reports referenced by ticket
notes: We should align scoring weights with Sales for enterprise SLAs — early feedback suggests increasing SLA weight for audited customers
Consider a lightweight ML classifier to detect 'breaking-API' patterns from model metadata (follow-up ENG spike)
Design will add a triage banner in the catalog request modal to explain auto-defer reasons
